subject: Annual invoicing swap: performance ratchet, safety-net credits, and migration milestones
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Li <ethan.li@acmeai.com>, AcmeAI Procurement <procurement@acmeai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Annual invoicing swap: performance ratchet, safety-net credits, and migration milestones

Ethan — thanks again for the time this morning. Per our discussion, I pulled together a concise proposal for switching AcmeAI from your current monthly billing to an annual prepay (12-month) model while preserving operational flexibility during the first 3 quarters. Key asks from our side and options for you are below.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Target: swap to a single annual invoice (12-month prepay) starting Jan 1, 2027.
- Pricing: step discounting based on committed annual $ (Tier A/B/C), with a 6% base term discount at $1.2M annual commit, up to 12% for higher tiers.
- Ramp protection: staged usage true-up (quarterly) for first 3 quarters, plus a 10% safety-net credit pool to handle under-commit risk.
- Performance ratchet: if monthly usage exceeds committed baseline by >25% for 2 consecutive months, pricing re-eval clause (upside rebate or model swap) — protects both sides.

Attachments: RDW-Acme_AnnualPricing_Options.xlsx (pricing bands + example cashflow) and Acme_Onboarding_Milestones.pdf (ops timeline).

As next steps, if the high-level looks ok, Ben can outline the exact discount matrix and finance constraints; Marissa will confirm onboarding milestones and SLAs required to guarantee capacity during ramp. I recommend we run a 3-month canary (no additional charge) post-conversion to validate latency and quota behavior.

Specific questions from your procurement checklist we covered but want to confirm:
1) Do you need monthly usage reporting + invoice-level true-up frequency (we suggested quarterly true-ups for Y1)?
2) Is AcmeAI able to accept a single annual invoice or do you require split invoices (e.g., 4 quarterly invoices) for internal CAPEX/OPEX cadence?
3) Any required contract term language around ramp safety-nets we should draft now (e.g., guaranteed minimal capacity, SLA credits)?

Happy to get Ben and Karthik to the thread on the discount math and to produce a one-page MSA addendum for procurement.

Cheers,

Laura Bennett
Senior Director, Sales — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Annual invoicing swap: performance ratchet, safety-net credits, and migration milestones

Laura — thanks for the clear summary and the docs. A few procurement/finance clarifications from our side:

1) Invoice cadence: our finance team prefers either a single annual invoice (preferred for discounting) or 4 equal quarterly invoices tied to the annual commitment. We cannot accept monthly invoices for the prepay.
2) True-up cadence: quarterly true-ups are acceptable, but we need clear crediting rules if we under-utilize in Q1/Q2 (how the safety-net credits are applied and expiration).
3) Ramp protection: can you clarify how the 10% safety-net credit pool is consumed? For example, if we commit $1.2M and use only $900k in year 1, what's the credit/refund flow?
4) Contract language: procurement will need a section that explicitly allows us to revert to a monthly plan at any point during year 1 if our product roadmap materially changes — with a defined unwind cost.

Also, three quick ops questions for Marissa:
- Does Redwood require IP allowlisting or network changes for the initial 30-day canary?
- What monitoring/dashboard links will be provided for token-level spend?
- Who is our single point of contact for incidents during the migration?

If these are reasonable, procurement is comfortable moving to a term sheet. We will need a draft term sheet with explicit payment milestones and a sample true-up calculation.

Best,
Ethan

Subject: Re: Annual invoicing swap: performance ratchet, safety-net credits, and migration milestones

Ethan — hi, I pulled together the specific commercial mechanics you asked for. See the short answers + worked example below. I'll attach the pricing workbook to the HubSpot deal shortly (and copied into the RDW sheet).

Quick answers:
- Invoice cadence: We can support 1x annual invoice or 4x quarterly invoices (equal amortized) for accounting. We cannot do >4 split invoices for prepay.
- Safety-net credits: The safety-net is a non-refundable credit pool applied to future usage within the 12-month term. Example: $1.2M commit with 10% safety-net = $120k credit reserve. If actual consumption = $900k, then $120k credits reduce unused balance but are not refundable; remaining unused credit expires at term-end unless agreed otherwise. We can convert unused credits to a one-time rebate of up to 50% of unused credits if there is a documented force majeure or product roadmap change (to be negotiated).
- True-up: Quarterly true-ups (30 days after quarter-end). If usage > committed run-rate by >20% cumulatively, then an overage charge at agreed overage rate applies. If usage < committed by >20% at quarter true-up, unused committed dollars are consumed by safety-net credits first.

Worked example (12-month commit = $1.2M; monthly committed run-rate = $100k):
Q1 actual usage = $80k/mo -> $240k total; safety-net draws $30k (10% of $300k quarterly run-rate) to bridge.
Q2 actual usage = $120k/mo -> $360k total; Q2 overage reconciles at true-up. At year end any remaining safety-net balance expires (or converted per escape clause).

Performance ratchet clause idea: If actual usage exceeds committed run-rate by >25% over any sliding 60-day window, Redwood and AcmeAI will meet to either (a) credit Acme at a 5% overage rebate for those months if Redwood is unable to meet latency/capacity SLAs, or (b) move Acme to the next tier pricing (if capacity costs materially increase). This gives both sides a clear remediation path.

Next steps from finance: if you confirm invoice cadence (1x vs 4x), I'll draft a payment schedule and a sample invoice. If you need refundable structure instead of credits, that will change discount levels (we can show both options in the workbook).

-Ben

Ethan — hi, Marissa from CS here. Quick operational notes so procurement knows what to expect during the migration/canary: 

1) Allowlisting / Networking: We typically ask for our egress IP ranges for allowlisting during the 30-day canary; no client-side infra changes are required beyond standard firewall rules. We will send the IP list and a short runbook.
2) Monitoring / dashboard: Redwood provides a token-level spending dashboard (read-only link) and an exportable daily usage CSV. We'll provision a dashboard user by day 0 of the canary and share SSO instructions.
3) SPOC for incidents: You will have a named Technical Account Manager (TAM) and a 24/7 on-call escalation pager if you choose the enterprise support add-on. For the canary we will assign a TAM (we propose Priya N. as TAM) and share their contact.
4) Onboarding milestones: see attached Acme_Onboarding_Milestones.pdf — proposed timeline
   - Week 0: Legal & billing sign-off; exchange of PO or PO number if needed.
   - Week 1-2: Allowlisting + canary config.
   - Week 3-6: Canary (production traffic but limited routing to reserved pool); capacity validation and latency tests.
   - Week 7: Full cutover and 30-day post-cutover monitoring window.

If procurement requires the ability to unwind to monthly within Y1, we can operationalize an unwind plan (takes ~5 business days to reconfigure routing and allocate on-demand capacity) — we will include an unwind cost schedule in the MSA addendum.

Happy to present this timeline to your engineering procurement group next week; let me know a few time slots.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0202

Team — this is helpful and addresses most of our concerns. A few confirmations before procurement signs off:

- Invoice cadence: AcmeAI will take the single annual invoice (preferred). Please provide the amortized quarterly invoice copy for our internal reporting (Ben, please prepare).
- Safety-net: the non-refundable credit pool is acceptable if there is an explicit conversion clause (the 50% convert-to-rebate option Ben mentioned) — procurement wants the conversion guardrails in the term sheet.
- Unwind: procurement accepts an unwind plan with a defined cost schedule. Please include a 5-business-day operational timeline and an unwind fee table in the MSA addendum.

Next steps: Laura — please send a one-page term sheet with the above mechanics and Ben's sample amortized invoice. Marissa — schedule a 30-minute call next Tuesday with our head of engineering for the canary runbook review. We will route the term sheet through our legal for a quick redline.

If we can get the term sheet by EOD tomorrow, procurement will aim to issue the PO by Oct 22.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this live.

Ethan
